mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_PANTS + i from PantMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 141), so file 03 is pants index 2, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Pad Pants. mu.db agrees: code 4610, group 9 index 2, Player/PantMale03.bmd.
why_this_one: Pasi's +0 line, and the Dark Wizard's first set. The mage stocks all five Pad pieces at +0 and only the gloves and boots were built, so three of his five lines were dropped by Realm.Shelf. See shared/Market.Mage.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel: nothing in this set is a forged plate. See profiles/soft_armour.json, which exists for these three sets.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 1, 0, 0 - the Dark Wizard alone.

sheet_from: Data/Player/lower_04_m.OZJ (128x128), lower_04b_m.OZT (32x32), hide.jpg and lower_04c.OZT (32x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names lower_04_m.jpg, lower_04b_m.tga, hide.jpg and lower_04c.tga; 94 of the 132 triangles are on the first, 4 on lower_04b_m, 12 on hide and 22 on lower_04c.
sheet_note: lower_04_m is the padded skirt and both legs, olive cloth panelled with gilt knotwork and a row of hanging tabs at the hem. Mean (76, 58, 38) at chroma 38. lower_04b_m and lower_04c are two more 32-squares of the same gold knotwork - the belt plate and the hip tabs - and neither cuts anything: both are .OZT with a full alpha channel, which is MU shipping a small ornament in the format that carries one and using none of it. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square, as on ArmorMale10.
material_note: Four islands, and unlike the jerkin this piece really does carry plate. Island 0 is 106 triangles - the padded skirt, both legs and hide's caps - and takes cloth. Islands 1 and 2 are two triangles each, which is lower_04b_m's 4 exactly: the belt plate, a 32-square of gold knotwork with nothing else on it. Island 3 is 22 triangles, which is lower_04c's 22 exactly: the row of gilt tabs at the hip. Those three take brass, the same cast yellow metal the Pad Gloves and Boots take, and here it is exact rather than a majority reading - each of the three islands is one ornament sheet and no cloth is inside it.
